automaticOutputs: Display anonymous counts of unlocked ships and their visible modernization yields.
manualInputs: The user confirms that each selected material ship is not rare, unique, quest-required, or intentionally retained.
prohibitedInferences: Never label a ship safe to consume from lock state, duplicate count, or modernization yield alone.
Never select or rank material ships automatically.

rubrics.fallback: Show the material-safety checklist and omit ship-specific consumption advice.
acceptanceTests: An unlocked duplicate is never described as safe to consume.
Unknown inventory state still produces a non-empty checklist.

automaticOutputs: Block sortie guidance on heavy damage, missing supply, or unavailable repair-state inputs.
Report damage, supply, and repair facts separately.
manualInputs: Material safety is confirmed only when the recommendation involves modernization.
prohibitedInferences: Never use a modernization-material check to declare a sortie fleet safe.
Never collapse an unknown component into a healthy state.

rubrics.fallback: Keep executable sortie advice blocked and show the unresolved safety checks.
acceptanceTests: Any heavy-damage signal blocks executable sortie advice.
Unknown damage or supply state cannot produce a safe label.
A non-modernization recommendation does not require material selection.

automaticOutputs: Show only quests present in the current live or cached local view and prerequisite edges whose reviewed status permits automatic reasoning.

Emit separate view-coverage and graph-coverage labels. View coverage must distinguish live-all-tabs, live-partial-tabs, cached-session, and unknown; graph coverage must distinguish reviewed-complete, reviewed-partial, and unresolved.
manualInputs: The user opens every relevant quest tab in the current session when a complete current-availability check is required.
prohibitedInferences: Never treat a quest missing from a partial or cached list as completed, unavailable, or not required.
Never invent a hidden prerequisite or promote an unregistered, disputed, or unresolved edge.
Never collapse current-view completeness and curated-graph completeness into one complete label.

rubrics.fallback: If a visible unlock quest exists, show it as current-view-only. Otherwise show the exact data-acquisition step to open all quest tabs and refresh the guide. Keep the chain partial and never return an empty plan.
acceptanceTests: A quest missing from a partial-tab or cached list remains unknown and is never described as completed.
A reviewed-complete graph with partial current-view coverage is not labeled complete.
Live all-tab coverage with an unresolved or unregistered edge is labeled graph-partial.
No visible quest produces a non-empty data-acquisition step rather than an empty plan.
A cached quest list is visibly distinguished from live all-tab data.

automaticOutputs: Display current local resource totals with an explicit freshness state and an optional trend whose observation window is shown.
Use measured, unknown, or stale as the only automatic resource-state labels. Do not emit low, medium, or high.
manualInputs: The user selects the current goal and a conserve, balanced, or spend posture. The posture expresses preference only and does not prove affordability.
prohibitedInferences: Never apply an unapproved low, medium, or high threshold.
Never infer willingness to spend resources from inventory totals.
Never infer map, EO, sortie, or event affordability from totals or user posture alone.
Never treat missing or stale totals as zero.

rubrics.fallback: When totals or posture are missing or stale, keep the posture unset, show the exact step to open or refresh the local resource view, and present only non-executable conservation checks. Do not produce a sortie route.
acceptanceTests: The same resource total can produce different preference annotations under different user postures without changing safety or route eligibility.
Zero, maximum, and exact boundary-looking totals remain measured facts and are not assigned an unapproved band.
Missing or stale totals remain unknown or stale and never become zero.
A selected spend posture cannot by itself produce an executable sortie or EO recommendation.

automaticOutputs: Show anonymous ship-type, level, ASW-stat, compatibility, and ASW-equipment category facts with an explicit freshness state.
Describe zero sonar or zero depth-charge ownership as category absent, not as a universal readiness gap.
manualInputs: The user selects the target map or mechanic before any target-specific check is requested.
The user confirms the intended fleet when local compatibility for that fleet cannot be established.
prohibitedInferences: Never apply one universal ASW-ready threshold.
Never treat target selection alone as sufficient evidence for readiness.
Never equate equipment ownership or equipped-category counts with compatibility for the intended fleet.
Never claim that an absent ASW category makes a route impossible without a reviewed target-specific rule.

rubrics.fallback: Show the measured ASW facts and the exact steps to select a target map or mechanic and inspect the intended fleet. Without a reviewed, versioned target rule, do not emit an ASW readiness verdict.
acceptanceTests: Zero sonar or depth-charge ownership is labeled category absent without claiming that a specific route is impossible.
No target map produces facts and a manual selection step, not a readiness verdict.
A selected target with no reviewed target-specific rule still produces no readiness verdict.
Owned ASW equipment that is incompatible with the intended fleet cannot produce a ready label.
Unknown or stale ship, equipment, or fleet data cannot produce a ready label.

evidence.symbol: ApiShip ASW state and SlotitemType ASW categories

automaticOutputs: Report ship-type, air-equipment, and LOS-equipment category presence or absence with explicit freshness.
Keep category presence, quantity, quality, air-power calculation, and map-specific LOS calculation as separate facts or checks.
manualInputs: The user selects a target map and, when applicable, the route variant, difficulty, and intended air-state goal before target-specific sufficiency is requested.
prohibitedInferences: Never label non-zero category ownership sufficient for a map.
Never label an absent category a target-specific gap without a reviewed target rule.
Never replace a map-specific LOS or air-power calculation with inventory counts.
Never treat target-map selection alone as evidence that the required route, formula, or threshold is known.

rubrics.fallback: Show category presence and absence, ask which capability and target context the user wants to inspect, and show a data-acquisition step when reviewed route or formula knowledge is unavailable. Do not select a sortie route.
acceptanceTests: A non-zero fighter count does not automatically produce air readiness.
An absent category is shown as a fact and is not automatically declared required for the target.
A selected map without a reviewed route, air-state target, or LOS formula remains insufficient.
An exact boundary-looking value cannot be classified while the applicable versioned formula is unavailable.
Unknown or stale ship and equipment inputs cannot produce a sufficient label.

automaticOutputs: List unlocked EO from the existing EO catalog as identity and unlock facts with explicit freshness.
Show current measured resources, damage, and capability facts separately without producing an affordability conclusion.
manualInputs: The user selects one EO, the current goal, resource posture, available time, and willingness to accept repair cost. These inputs express preference and constraints only.
prohibitedInferences: Never infer affordability or safety from EO unlock state.
Never infer current affordability from a prior clear or historical success.
Never infer affordability from resource posture alone.
Never recommend all unlocked EO by default.
Never create an EO route without separately reviewed, versioned, and unexpired route knowledge and current required inputs.

rubrics.fallback: Present unlocked EO only as optional long-term targets. Show the exact unresolved safety, resource, capability, route, or time check and the local screen needed to obtain it. Alternative normal-map, practice, or expedition items must be presented as checks or data-acquisition steps unless their own current conditions are verified.
acceptanceTests: An unlocked EO with unknown or failed safety, resources, capability, route, or time constraints remains optional and non-executable.
A previous clear, when separately evidenced, is displayed only as historical evidence and never as a guarantee.
No reviewed route knowledge produces no route instructions.
A selected resource posture cannot by itself produce an affordability verdict.
An unlocked EO that is unsuitable for the current fleet produces an explicit blocker and a non-empty alternative check.
Unknown or stale map unlock data produces a map-screen data-acquisition step rather than an EO list.

automaticOutputs: Show anonymous ship-type, level-band, equipment-category, and resource coverage facts with explicit freshness.
Label the result evergreen coverage and never event readiness.
manualInputs: The user selects whether event participation is a current goal and chooses one evergreen capability category to inspect next.
prohibitedInferences: Never declare event-ready from evergreen breadth alone.
Never accept user-entered free text as a substitute for a reviewed event overlay.
Never infer event difficulty, routing, locks, bonuses, or ship preservation requirements without a reviewed, versioned, and unexpired overlay.
Never rank a category as the most important deficiency without an independently approved evergreen breadth rubric.

rubrics.fallback: Show evergreen category coverage and one explicit manual next step: ask the user to choose a category to inspect. When event participation is selected but no valid overlay exists, state that event-specific guidance is unavailable and return to evergreen preparation without an event-readiness conclusion.
acceptanceTests: No event overlay produces no event-ready label and a non-empty evergreen manual-check outcome.
An expired, malformed, or unreviewed overlay cannot produce event-specific advice.
A broad fleet can still be shown as having unknown event suitability.
Selecting an event goal cannot bypass the overlay requirement.
Without an approved breadth rubric, no category is automatically called the highest-priority deficiency.
